nodes.name: Lead Intake Webhook
nodes.notes: POST /lead-intake. Header X-Lead-Engine-Secret must match $env.LEAD_ENGINE_SECRET. Responds only after a Respond To Webhook node runs.

nodes.name: Valid Ingress Secret?
nodes.notes: Security gate BEFORE any Google Sheets lookup or business logic. Missing or wrong secret -> 401 branch.

nodes.name: Respond 401 Invalid Secret
nodes.notes: Never reveal what the secret is or hint at business data.

nodes.name: Get Business Config
nodes.notes: Reads ALL business_config rows (read-all-then-filter retained deliberately; correctness over premature optimization). The Code node enforces an exact business_id match so a lead can never be matched against another business's config.

nodes.name: Resolve Config & Normalize Lead
nodes.notes: V4.3: builds the canonical lead, computes urgency + 0-100 score (prioritization heuristic, not revenue prediction), merges business config, derives a deterministic idempotency_key, validates the booking link (HTTPS-only; javascript:/data:/file:/other schemes and malformed URLs are rejected as absent), and emits HTML-escaped copies (_esc_*) for email templates.

nodes.name: Business Valid & Active?
nodes.notes: Rejects unknown or inactive businesses. Optional config fields (customer email, owner email, booking link) are intentionally NOT required here.

nodes.name: Check Duplicate
nodes.notes: V4.2: duplicate order idempotency_key+business_id, then source_id+source_type+business_id, then phone+business_id, then email+business_id (all tenant-scoped). Phone compared via digits-only normalization. Retry-aware but NOT transactionally race-safe under concurrent requests.

nodes.name: Is Duplicate?
nodes.notes: V4 FIX: branch polarity corrected. TRUE (duplicate) -> Respond 200 Duplicate Accepted; FALSE (new) -> Append Lead. In V3 these were inverted, so duplicates would be re-appended and new leads mis-labeled as duplicates.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ status: 'accepted', duplicate: true, reason: $json._duplicateReason, lead_id: $json.lead_id, code: 200 }) }}

nodes.name: Respond 200 Duplicate Accepted
nodes.notes: Idempotent: retries of the same event do not create a second lead.

nodes.name: Compute Next Follow-up
nodes.notes: V4: reads authoritative data from 'Check Duplicate' (immune to Google Sheets node output shape). Sets next_followup_at = now + business followup_delay_hours (default 24h). Does NOT depend on email success.

nodes.name: Update Lead Next Follow-up
nodes.notes: Persists the first next_followup_at for the sweeper. The webhook response path and the email side effects both branch from this node and are independent of one another.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ status: 'created', lead_id: $('Compute Next Follow-up').first().json.lead_id, score: $('Compute Next Follow-up').first().json.score, urgency: $('Compute Next Follow-up').first().json.urgency, code: 200 }) }}

nodes.name: Respond 200 Created
nodes.notes: V4: terminal success response after follow-up persistence. Email side effects branch after persistence and are independent of the webhook response path. Does NOT claim an email was delivered.

nodes.name: Prepare Email Content
nodes.notes: V4 (new): re-emits the fully enriched lead (canonical + config + _esc_* fields) so the email branches do not depend on the Google Sheets node output shape.

nodes.name: Skip Customer Email
nodes.notes: V4 (new): terminal no-op for the no-customer-email branch.

parameters.subject: ={{ ' We received your request — ' + $json.business_name }}
parameters.html:
={{ `

Hi ${$json._esc_name || 'there'},

Thanks for contacting ${$json._esc_business_name}. We received your request${$json.service ? ' regarding ' + $json._esc_service + '' : ''} and a member of our team will be in touch.

${$json.booking_link ? '

You can book online now: Schedule here

' : ''}

Replying to this email reaches our team directly.

— ${$json._esc_business_name}

` }}

nodes.name: Customer Acknowledgment
nodes.notes: V4: non-critical side effect. onError=continueErrorOutput isolates SMTP failure: error output routes to a sanitized errors-sheet log; lead persistence / follow-up / response already completed.

nodes.name: End Customer Email
nodes.notes: V4 (new): terminal no-op for the customer-email success output.

nodes.name: Build Customer Email Error Record
nodes.notes: V4 (new): captures + sanitizes a customer email failure into an errors-sheet record. No secrets ever stored or emailed.

nodes.name: Append Customer Email Error
nodes.notes: V4 (new): failure-isolation sink for customer email failures. If this append itself fails, the workflow-level error handler (06) captures it.

nodes.name: Skip Owner Email
nodes.notes: V4 (new): terminal no-op for the no-owner-email branch.

nodes.name: Owner Notification
nodes.notes: V4: non-critical side effect. onError=continueErrorOutput isolates SMTP failure; lead stays valid. User-provided fields are HTML-escaped.

nodes.name: End Owner Email
nodes.notes: V4 (new): terminal no-op for the owner-email success output.

nodes.name: Build Owner Email Error Record
nodes.notes: V4 (new): captures + sanitizes an owner email failure into an errors-sheet record.

nodes.name: Append Owner Email Error
nodes.notes: V4 (new): failure-isolation sink for owner email failures. Separate append node per email avoids double-execution convergence.

nodes.name: Read Existing Leads
nodes.notes: Loads existing leads for the idempotency / duplicate check.

nodes.name: Append Lead
nodes.notes: Persistence-first: the lead row is written here, BEFORE any email side effects. Column headers in the leads tab must match the canonical lead keys so autoMapInputData writes correctly.
